summary: India's central bank raised its repo rate 0.25 point to 5.50% on Oct 7, its first hike since February 2023, as oil above $100 pushed inflation up. September consumer inflation was 5.54%, above the RBI's 5.2% forecast. On Oct 29 the Sensex jumped 905.01 points to 74,151.04 and the Nifty 1.05% to 22,936.75 on bank and consumer buying after the Fed's pause (Deccan Herald), and the rupee firmed 3 paise to 95.25 per dollar (Economic Times). Lower oil this week helps India, which imports most of its crude. A 10% US Section 301 tariff still applies to most Indian goods, and the February trade deal has stalled.
for_you: India helps outsourcers (INFY, WIT) through a weak rupee and hurts banks and travel through higher rates. Nothing here is on your lists; low priority.

watch.name: RBI repo rate
watch.why: Hiked 0.25 point, stance changed to calibrated tightening. Another hike in December is expected by Nomura and SBI.

watch.name: Rupees per US dollar
watch.why: Up 3 paise on the day (Economic Times). Near record weakness.

watch.name: BSE Sensex
watch.why: Up 905.01 points on bank and consumer buying after the Fed paused (Deccan Herald).

watch.name: US tariff on Indian goods
watch.why: Section 301 tariff on most goods. Services like IT are not tariffed.

watch.name: 10 year government bond yield
watch.why: Highest since October 2023 after the RBI hike; higher yields hurt bank bond holdings and growth stocks.

changes.what: The RBI raised the repo rate to 5.50% in a unanimous vote and raised its inflation forecast to 5.2%. Tighter money is a headwind for Indian banks and consumer stocks.

The RBI moved to curb dollar demand in the spot market and the rupee rebounded about 1% to near 95.7 per dollar, but the Sensex fell about 0.8% by midday as bond yields rose for a fourth session and foreign outflows kept building.
changes.for_you: No action. Indian bank ADRs stay under pressure from rising yields. INFY and WIT are left out because a firmer rupee trims their edge but they are not on a setup list.

changes.what: India's 10 year bond yield rose to 7.37% on Oct 12, its highest since October 2023, even as the rupee bounced about 1% to near 95.76 per dollar on the RBI's new curbs. Bloomberg called the curbs among the strongest currency defenses since the 2013 taper tantrum.
changes.for_you: No action. Indian bank ADRs face higher funding costs and bond losses. INFY is left out of both lists: a weak rupee helps it, but the rupee just bounced.

changes.what: India's September consumer prices rose 5.54% from a year ago, up from 4.83% in August, with food up 7.74% (MoSPI, Oct 12). Inflation is now above the RBI's own 5.2% forecast, which backs its Oct 7 hike and keeps another one possible.
changes.for_you: No action; nothing here is on your lists. INDA rose 1.9% on Oct 15 but its up/down volume is 0.70, so sellers still lead.

changes.what: On Oct 16 Trump waived the Graham Act's tariffs of up to 100% on the top five buyers of Russian crude, two days before they took effect. India is one of the largest buyers, so the threat of a new US tariff on top of the 10% Section 301 rate is gone for now, and Brent fell about 2% to $107.60 on Oct 19, which helps an oil importer.
changes.for_you: No action. INDA (47.66) is still in a downtrend with up/down volume 0.69, so a better headline is not a buy signal yet. HDB and IBN are left out: lower oil helps, but rates are still rising.

changes.what: The Sensex rose 905.01 points to 74,151.04 and the Nifty 1.05% to 22,936.75 on Oct 29 after the Fed held, led by banks and consumer stocks (Deccan Herald); the rupee closed at 95.25 per dollar (Economic Times). Brent easing toward $113 helps an oil importer.
changes.for_you: No action. INDA closed at 46.79 on Oct 28 (Massive) and has no verdict; one strong day does not end a downtrend.
